key_insight: How an agent expresses and executes robot actions can substantially change task success, even when perception and control stay fixed.
engineering_relevance: Robot-use interfaces should reduce unnecessary agent decisions while preserving essential feedback to improve execution reliability.
method: Introduce RUIBench: 30 manipulation tasks across five suites.
Develop RUIKit: 13 interfaces spanning six action abstractions and two interaction forms.
Compare interfaces under shared perception and control in simulation.
evidence_signal: Changing only the interface shifted simulated success rates from 45% to 81% for a frontier agent and from 13% to 47% for a fine-tuned 4B model.
watch_item: Agents frequently declared success despite observable failures, highlighting the need for task-level verification beyond individual actions.
paper_title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
